\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Programs.Light.Compiler.Dispatcher}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Dispatcher extension by one case]
\lean{Light.Compiler.dispatcher_succ}
\label{Light.Compiler.dispatcher_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.cONE, Light.Compiler.cRR, Light.Compiler.dispatcher}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, the dispatcher with $n+1$ cases is the dispatcher with $n$
cases followed by the instruction that decrements the return register and the
instruction that branches to position $n$ when that register is negative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the Dispatcher]
\lean{Light.Compiler.length_dispatcher}
\label{Light.Compiler.length_dispatcher}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.dispatcher}
\difficulty{1}
For every $n\in\mathbb N$, the dispatcher built from $n$ entries has length $2n$
instructions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dispatcher prefix property]
\lean{Light.Compiler.dispatcher_prefix}
\label{Light.Compiler.dispatcher_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.dispatcher, Light.Compiler.dispatcher_succ}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $j$ and $n$ with $j\le n$, the dispatcher containing $j$ cases is a
prefix of the dispatcher containing $n$ cases.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Individual Dispatcher Entries]
\lean{Light.Compiler.codeAt_dispatcher}
\label{Light.Compiler.codeAt_dispatcher}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.cONE, Light.Compiler.cRR, Light.Compiler.dispatcher, Light.Compiler.dispatcher_prefix, Light.Compiler.dispatcher_succ, Light.Compiler.length_dispatcher, WordRAM.CodeAt, WordRAM.CodeAt.cast_pos, WordRAM.CodeAt.right}
\difficulty{4}
Let $code$ be a finite instruction list and $disp,n$ natural numbers. If the dispatcher
for $n$ procedures is a prefix of the code beginning at $disp$, then for every $j<n$,
the decrement-and-branch pair for procedure $j$ is a prefix of the code beginning at
$disp+2j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One dispatcher comparison step]
\lean{Light.Compiler.steps_dispatcher_pair}
\label{Light.Compiler.steps_dispatcher_pair}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.cONE, Light.Compiler.cRR, Light.Compiler.codeAt_dispatcher, Light.Compiler.dispatcher, WordRAM.CodeAt, WordRAM.CodeAt.tail, WordRAM.InRange, WordRAM.Steps, WordRAM.Steps.trans, WordRAM.steps_bltz, WordRAM.steps_sub, WordRAM.wd}
\difficulty{4}
Let the dispatcher for $n$ procedures occur at position $\mathrm{disp}$ in a word-RAM
program of word size $W$. If $j<n$, the one-register contains the word encoding $1$, and
$v-1$ lies in the signed range $-2^{W-1}\le v-1<2^{W-1}$, then from program counter
$\mathrm{disp}+2j$ with the return-register containing the word encoding $v$, two
machine steps reach a configuration whose return-register contains the word encoding
$v-1$. Its program counter is $j$ if $v-1<0$, and otherwise is $\mathrm{disp}+2(j+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dispatcher progress from an offset]
\lean{Light.Compiler.steps_dispatcher_from}
\label{Light.Compiler.steps_dispatcher_from}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.cONE, Light.Compiler.cRR, Light.Compiler.dispatcher, Light.Compiler.steps_dispatcher_pair, WordRAM.CodeAt, WordRAM.Steps, WordRAM.Steps.cast_count, WordRAM.Steps.cast_pos, WordRAM.Steps.trans, WordRAM.wd}
\difficulty{5}
Let the dispatcher for $n$ procedures occur at position $\mathrm{disp}$ in a word-RAM
program of word size $W$, and suppose the code there begins with that dispatcher. If
$2n<2^W$, the one-register contains the word encoding $1$, and $j+k<n$, then from
program counter $\mathrm{disp}+2j$ with the return-register containing the word encoding
$k$, after $2(k+1)$ machine steps the program counter is $j+k$ and the return-register
contains the word encoding $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dispatcher selects a procedure]
\lean{Light.Compiler.steps_dispatcher}
\label{Light.Compiler.steps_dispatcher}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Compiler.cONE, Light.Compiler.cRR, Light.Compiler.dispatcher, Light.Compiler.steps_dispatcher_from, WordRAM.CodeAt, WordRAM.Steps, WordRAM.wd}
\difficulty{3}
Let the dispatcher for $n$ procedures occur at position $\mathrm{disp}$ in a word-RAM
program of word size $W$, and suppose the code there begins with that dispatcher. If
$r<n$, $2n<2^W$, the one-register contains the word encoding $1$, and the
return-register contains the word encoding $r$, then after $2(r+1)$ machine steps the
program counter is $r$ and the return-register contains the word encoding $-1$.
\end{theorem}
